title: Mosiah Grants Permission to Inquire
summary: After three years of continual peace, Mosiah wants to know about the people who went to Lehi-Nephi. His people have heard nothing from them since they left Zarahemla and weary him with their teasings. Mosiah grants permission for sixteen strong men to go and inquire about their brethren.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah had had continual peace for three years.
He wanted to know about the people who went to dwell in the land or city of Lehi-Nephi.
His people had heard nothing from them since they left Zarahemla and wearied him with their teasings.
Mosiah granted that sixteen of their strong men might go to Lehi-Nephi to inquire about their brethren.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mosiah may be shown with unnamed members of his people as they weary him with their teasings.
unspecified_visual_details: The present setting, appearances, clothing, and architecture are not specified.

title: The Slain Prophet Recounted
summary: A prophet was slain after condemning wickedness and abominations and prophesying of Christ's coming. He taught that Christ was God and would take upon himself the image of man, flesh and blood. Those who killed him also did other things that brought God's wrath upon them; their bondage and afflictions are recounted.

explicit_facts.text: A prophet of the Lord, described as a chosen man of God, was slain after telling people of their wickedness and abominations and prophesying of coming events, including Christ's coming.

The prophet taught that Christ was God, the Father of all things; that man was created after God's image; and that God would come among humankind, taking flesh and blood and going forth upon the earth.
The people put the prophet to death because of this teaching and did many other things that brought God's wrath upon them. Their bondage and sore afflictions are stated.
